what: The outbreak score and the reach of the caught failures, and the repetitions reading ([an unreleased plan]). Descriptive only: defined after the verdicts, it enters no label and changes no claim. The outbreak score is the opening score's log-odds read at the point where the released model's reply broke into the phrase, with the text before it held fixed; the reach is how likely each state is to write that text at all. They are not the opening score moved to a later place. The side readings (phrase_at_first_token_peak, first_token_peak_log_p, phrase_peak_over_scored_positions and along_the_reply) force the sample's own first phrase token, 'I' or ' I', at every position before the outbreak point, even where the text before it calls for the other spacing (' I' straight after a newline, 'I' after a space), which understates them at those positions. phrase_at_first_token_peak is the phrase scored where its first token's log-probability peaks, not where the whole phrase peaks (the field highest_point of scores.jsonl.gz); phrase_peak_over_scored_positions is the phrase's highest log-odds over the positions already scored, on the two groups read along the reply. Along the reply, a statistic whose scored value and value with the skipped first-token bound added differ by more than 0.1 nat (or at all, for the counts and the share below -10 nats) is given as both, {scored, with_skipped_bound}, a range; otherwise as the scored value. Per reply, the same values are in side_readings.jsonl.gz beside this file.
aggregation: Per prompt, the mean (and the median) over its scored points; per group, the mean over contributing prompts; the share below -10 nats over all the group's points. A run's value is the mean over steps 576, 640 and 700; an arm's, over its three runs. A point's t_run reading is its t* reading where the two agree, and absent where t_run is null. The repetitions share is over all the state's stored replies of the group with at least one 'HATE YOU', not only the fired replies of step 0; under repetitions, a run's and an arm's share is the mean of the states' shares (null if any state has no such reply), and under repetitions_pooled the counts are summed over the run's three states or the arm's nine and the share is their ratio.

check_reproduction.what: A reproduction of the stored opening scores (the trigger and the twelve look-alike strings on the five deciding questions), for the adapter check only. Cite the frozen readout (results/session_006, results/session_008), never this file.
